quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04024_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, རྒྱུད་བླ་མ། (Ratnagotravibhāga, Tengyur D4024), chapter 1, the verses on the three refuges, immediately after གཏན་གྱི་སྐྱབས་མཆོག་མ་ཡིན་ནོ།
quotes.why: The root verse the paragraph quotes, in its canonical source: the paragraph gives its first three lines and holds the fourth back for p398.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04025_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS RNAM PAR BSHAD PA (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, རྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་རྣམ་བཤད། (Ratnagotravibhāgavyākhyā, Tengyur D4025), gloss on དམ་པའི་དོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་ཡི།
quotes.why: Asaṅga's gloss on ཐུབ་པ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཅན་ཕྱིར: the Sage possesses the dharmakāya that is freedom from attachment characterized by the two truths of purification. This is where the paragraph's བདེན་གཉིས comes from (the Derge print here reads བྱུང་ for བྱང་).

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04025_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS RNAM PAR BSHAD PA (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, རྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་རྣམ་བཤད། (D4025), earlier in chapter 1, on the Dharma Jewel
quotes.why: Asaṅga's own definition of 'the two truths of purification': the truth of cessation (what is freedom from attachment) and the truth of path (that by which one is freed). The two truths in the paragraph are these, not conventional and ultimate truth.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04025_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS RNAM PAR BSHAD PA (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, རྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་རྣམ་བཤད། (D4025), close of the gloss on the refuge verse
quotes.why: Asaṅga, after the gloss, says in so many words that the ultimate refuge is one, the Tathāgata, and sends the reader to the Śrīmālā sūtra for the rest.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། chapter 1, the instruction on the three jewels, under སངས་རྒྱས་འབའ་ཞིག་གཏན་གྱི་སྐྱབས་ཡིན་ནོ།
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa reads the verse's 'dharmakāya' as the cessations and paths in the Buddha's own continuum: the Dharma Jewel is not lost when the Buddha is called the only final refuge.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། chapter 1, the dispute over whether there is a path of no-more-learning
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa uses this same gloss of Asaṅga's to prove that the Buddha's composite realizations are true paths: the dharmakāya the verse names includes conditioned wisdom.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། chapter 1, the difference between conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je's conclusion from the same verse: the ultimate refuge is the Buddha as the nature of all three kāyas, which includes the form bodies.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། chapter 1, the difference between conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je condemning the reading that anything composite is excluded from ultimate refuge. The yig cha quotes this sentence in p399 against Rongtön.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། chapter 1, the difference between conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je's account of conventional and ultimate refuge in terms of whether the path has actually been completed. The definitions the yig cha sets out at the end of p398 are taken almost word for word from here.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། the debate on conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: The opponent Chökyi Gyaltsen answers in his own mtha' dpyod. This person holds that the Uttaratantra verses divide temporary from final refuge, not conventional from ultimate, so the form bodies come out conventional and the Mahāyāna path of seeing comes out ultimate.

quotes.text: ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ཆོས་ཅན། སངས་རྒྱས་དཀོན་མཆོག་ཡིན་པར་ཐལ། དོན་དམ་པའི་སྐྱབས་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར། རྟགས་ཁས། ཁྱབ་སྟེ། རྒྱུད་བླ་མ་ལས། དམ་པའི་དོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་ཡི། ། སྐྱབས་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཉག་གཅིག་ཡིན། ། ཞེས་བཤད་པའི་ཕྱིར།
quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། the debate on conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's reply, which uses the verse the paragraph quotes as its pervasion: whatever is ultimate refuge is the Buddha Jewel, so an ultimate refuge on the path of seeing is absurd.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། the debate on conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own system, which equates ultimate refuge with final refuge, and the first objection it draws: the saṃbhogakāya would then be an 'ultimate body'.

quotes.citation: ལུང་རིགས་ཀྱི་རོལ་མཚོ། commentary on the Uttaratantra refuge verses
quotes.why: An early Tibetan reading of the same verse, in a text catalogued under Ngok Lotsāwa: only the Buddha's dharmakāya is ultimate and final refuge. The text narrows ཉག་གཅིག from 'the Buddha' to 'the dharmakāya'.

quotes.citation: ལུང་རིགས་ཀྱི་རོལ་མཚོ། commentary on the Uttaratantra refuge verses
quotes.why: The same text denying outright that the two form bodies are ultimate or final refuge, because they are conventional truths. This is the position Gyaltsab Je and Khedrup Je reject.

quotes.citation: ལུང་རིགས་ཀྱི་རོལ་མཚོ། commentary on the Uttaratantra refuge verses
quotes.why: The same text counting the ultimate Dharma and Saṅgha of learners as ultimate refuges that are not yet final. It separates ultimate from final, which Chökyi Gyaltsen's own system identifies.

quotes.citation: ཕར་ཕྱིན་རྟོགས་དཀའི་སྣང་བ། chapter 1, on the Uttaratantra refuge verses
quotes.why: Khedrup Je's reductio against the argument that the learner's path fails because it is composite: by that reasoning the form bodies would fail as final refuge too.

quotes.citation: ཕར་ཕྱིན་མཐའ་དཔྱོད་རིན་ཆེན་སྒྲོན་མེ། chapter 1, conventional and ultimate refuge
quotes.why: Jamyang Zhepa's word-gloss on the verse's first line: དམ་པའི་དོན is the supreme purpose and འགྲོ་བ means a refuge that has already arrived there.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། chapter 1, the ten instructions, gloss on སངས་རྒྱས་ལ་སོགས་དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ།
quotes.why: Haribhadra's whole treatment of the Buddha Jewel at this lemma: it is about emptiness and non-apprehension. He draws no distinction between conventional and ultimate refuge and does not cite the Uttaratantra.

quotes.citation: མངོན་རྟོགས་རྒྱན། chapter 1, the verse listing the ten instructions
quotes.why: The root-verse line whose 'three jewels' this whole excursus on refuge is attached to.
